statements.impact_statement: GHSA-pmwq-pjrm-6p5r (GO-2026-5547; osv.dev lists no CVE alias): in-toto-golang before 0.11.0 used ^ for negation inside glob character classes in layout artifact rules, while in-toto-python uses !, so a layout written for one implementation can match different artifacts when verified by the other (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pmwq-pjrm-6p5r, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5547). The fix is https://github.com/in-toto/in-toto-golang/pull/462 (commit 36d782ffb2ca3adbffcdce1fd971c23319dd4469, which changes in_toto/match.go), released as v0.11.0; the affected code is the artifact-rule pattern matcher match() in the in_toto package, reached through layout verification (VerifyArtifacts). Checked every build-dev package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository on 2026-11-28: 92 versions, 2.6.4-r0 to the current 2.30.0-r1, each for x86_64 and aarch64, except 2.6.4-r0, which is published for aarch64 only. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/build, a statically linked Go program built for Linux (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies). We downloaded every package from 2.6.4-r0 to 2.16.8-r0 (38 versions) for both architectures, checked each against its index checksum, and read the Go build information and the function table (.gopclntab) of every program in it, plus 2.17.0-r0 and 2.30.0-r1 for both architectures. The in-toto-golang version in the build program is github.com/in-toto/in-toto-golang v0.9.0 in 2.6.4-r0 to 2.9.1-r0 and v0.10.0 in 2.9.2-r0 to 2.16.8-r0, and its build information has no replace directive for that module. None of these programs links any in-toto-golang code: no function in any of their function tables names github.com/in-toto/in-toto-golang, so neither the pattern matcher nor any layout verification is present (runtime.main is present in every program). From 2.17.0-r0 to 2.30.0-r1 the Go build information of /usr/bin/build records github.com/in-toto/in-toto-golang v0.11.0, the fixed release; we read it from every one of those packages (each matching its index checksum) on 2026-11-27 and re-read 2.17.0-r0 and 2.30.0-r1 on 2026-11-28. As a control, a static Go program built for linux/arm64 (CGO_ENABLED=0, -trimpath, -s -w) against in-toto-golang v0.10.0 that calls VerifyArtifacts shows match, matchChunk, verifyMatchRule and VerifyArtifacts among 39 in_toto functions in its function table, while one that only uses the in_toto Statement types shows none, so linked matcher code would be visible in this table. The builds that ship v0.9.0 or v0.10.0 therefore do not contain the vulnerable code, and the later builds ship the fixed release.

GHSA-pmwq-pjrm-6p5r (GO-2026-5547, no CVE id): in-toto-golang before 0.11.0 used ^ for negation inside glob character classes in layout artifact rules, while in-toto-python uses !, so a layout written for one implementation can match different artifacts when verified by the other (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pmwq-pjrm-6p5r, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5547). The fix is https://github.com/in-toto/in-toto-golang/pull/462 (commit 36d782ffb2ca3adbffcdce1fd971c23319dd4469), released as v0.11.0; the affected code is the artifact-rule pattern matcher in the in_toto package. Checked every scout-cli-dev package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository by 2026-11-27: 25 builds, 1.20.4-r1 to 1.30.0-r1, each for x86_64 and aarch64. Each holds one file, /usr/bin/docker-scout, the Docker Scout CLI, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 for GOOS=linux. The -dev build has the same Go release and module versions as the scout-cli build of the same version, built without the -w linker flag and without -trimpath. We downloaded all 50 of these packages (each matching its index checksum) and read the Go build information (go version -m) and the function table (go tool nm) of every program. The in-toto-golang version is github.com/in-toto/in-toto-golang v0.10.0 in 1.20.4-r1 to 1.20.4-r3; github.com/in-toto/in-toto-golang v0.11.0 in 1.20.4-r4 to 1.30.0-r1. No build links any in-toto-golang code: the only names under github.com/in-toto/in-toto-golang in any function table are compiler-generated type-equality functions for its SLSA provenance structures (type:.eq.github.com/in-toto/in-toto-golang/in_toto/slsa_provenance/v0%2e2.ProvenanceMetadata, type:.eq.github.com/in-toto/in-toto-golang/in_toto/slsa_provenance/v1.BuildMetadata), which compare struct fields and do not match artifact patterns; there is no in_toto package function at all, so neither the pattern matcher nor any layout verification is present (runtime.main is present in every program, as a control). The builds that ship v0.10.0 therefore do not contain the vulnerable code, and the later builds ship the fixed release. The advisory has no CVE id and no Debian tracker entry; this decision rests on the function tables above.

statements.impact_statement: GHSA-pmwq-pjrm-6p5r (GO-2026-5547, no CVE id): in-toto-golang before 0.11.0 used ^ for negation inside glob character classes in layout artifact rules, while in-toto-python uses !, so a layout written for one implementation can match different artifacts when verified by the other (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pmwq-pjrm-6p5r, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5547). The fix is https://github.com/in-toto/in-toto-golang/pull/462 (commit 36d782ffb2ca3adbffcdce1fd971c23319dd4469), released as v0.11.0; the affected code is the artifact-rule pattern matcher in the in_toto package. Checked every scout-cli package published for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository by 2026-11-27: 25 builds, 1.20.4-1 to 1.30.0-1, each for amd64 and arm64. Each package lists one file in its md5sums, /usr/bin/docker-scout, the Docker Scout CLI, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 for GOOS=linux. For every build that file has the same md5 as /usr/bin/docker-scout in the Alpine 3.23 scout-cli package of the same version and architecture (1.20.4-r1 for 1.20.4-1, and so on), so it is the same program; we downloaded every one of those Alpine packages (each matching its index checksum) and read the Go build information (go version -m) and the function table (go tool nm) of every program. The in-toto-golang version is github.com/in-toto/in-toto-golang v0.10.0 in 1.20.4-1 to 1.20.4-3; github.com/in-toto/in-toto-golang v0.11.0 in 1.20.4-4 to 1.30.0-1. No build links any in-toto-golang code: the only names under github.com/in-toto/in-toto-golang in any function table are compiler-generated type-equality functions for its SLSA provenance structures (type:.eq.github.com/in-toto/in-toto-golang/in_toto/slsa_provenance/v0%2e2.ProvenanceMetadata, type:.eq.github.com/in-toto/in-toto-golang/in_toto/slsa_provenance/v1.BuildMetadata), which compare struct fields and do not match artifact patterns; there is no in_toto package function at all, so neither the pattern matcher nor any layout verification is present (runtime.main is present in every program, as a control). The builds that ship v0.10.0 therefore do not contain the vulnerable code, and the later builds ship the fixed release. The advisory has no CVE id and no Debian tracker entry; this decision rests on the function tables above.
